title: Internalized Experience: How Training Data Shapes Memory Formation in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.28613v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Parametric memory enables large language models (LLMs) to retain information from past experience and reuse it in subsequent tasks. Yet how training data supports the internalization of reusable task rules remains unclear. We introduce FSMem (Finite-State Machine Memory), a state-transition framework for constructing training data and studying how data content and organization shape memory formation. We evaluate rule reuse across synthetic worlds, classical planning, and code execution through valid-action identification and execution-outcome prediction, complemented by next-operation prediction in code. Our experiments reveal several systematic learning patterns. Under matched training conditions, even unchanged task rules become harder to internalize when learned alongside a larger variety of action types; by contrast, scaling the training data to provide broader state-action coverage generally improves rule learning. translated_title: 内化经验：训练数据如何塑造大语言模型中的记忆形成
translated_abstract: 参数化记忆使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够保留过去经验中的信息，并在后续任务中加以复用。然而，训练数据如何支持可复用任务规则的内化仍不清楚。我们提出FSMem（有限状态机记忆），一个用于构建训练数据的状态转移框架，以研究数据内容与组织方式如何塑造记忆形成。我们通过有效动作识别和执行结果预测，在合成世界、经典规划和代码执行等场景中评估规则复用能力，并通过下一操作预测对代码场景进行补充评估。实验揭示了若干系统性的学习规律：在训练条件匹配的情况下，即使任务规则保持不变，当与更多种类的动作类型共同学习时，规则也会变得更难内化；相比之下，扩大训练数据规模以提供更广泛的状态-动作覆盖，通常能改善规则学习效果。我们进一步发现（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出FSMem状态转移框架以研究训练数据如何塑造大语言模型的参数化记忆形成，发现动作类型多样性会阻碍规则内化，而扩大状态-动作覆盖范围通常能提升规则学习能力。
en_tdlr: Proposes FSMem, a state-transition framework for studying how training data shapes parametric memory formation in LLMs, finding that diversity of action types hinders rule internalization, while broader state-action coverage generally improves rule learning.
